Nothing new is dispatched until you or Josh pick the next work.

Josh said go on a second bucket: add-linux-host section 1 (the first consumer of the host contract, on this host), add-policy-aware-audit, and add-executor-rendezvous (Bend only). Plans are being written. Items 2 to 7 still wait on you; the Windows and Drift hosts stay deferred until items 4 and 5 are answered.

fields.buckets_typing:
When buckets are typed, the bucket.
When buckets opt for anytype, the type
When buckets opt for notype, the record or fields within the record
When buckets opt for notype and contain files as an s3-compat bucket, well... duh.
fields.buckets_code:
Cryptographic signing determines who wrote code, who owns it is rather unimportant except as to whether they wish to obtain additional code or updates or perhaps to revoke their code. A bucket can come with a cryptographic author keypair for signing.

Code is 'ran' in a very interesting number of ways.
Code may be ran by the owner on the owner's hardware
Code may be ran by the system at the behest of the source data owner and the bucket owner to prove or be elected as the executor on the bucket for a while
Code may be ran by the data owner, they may be doing so for money or cooperation or as an IOU it can redeem.

The code attached to buckets still has to be given permissions in the system, so it's not exactly a simple 'where' so much as 'what the source allows' for execution. We actually also prefer computing near data as the bucket code is surely smaller than the source(s)
fields.buckets_views: Buckets aren't durables, they're runtime constructs. They don't influence storage and aren't necessarily stored in the main storage system though they may be materialized from disk later. They are absolutely view-ish, and bucket pay rules and everything works like http payment and s3 bucket payment configurating
fields.buckets_split: As much as we can make bend policyy we do, we use the runtime mechanism to actuate the system and do not put into the runtime mechanisms what belongs in bend policy.
